**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/03/27 (Mon) 10:14
- [USER] User requested an ice breaker activity to help participants relax at the beginning of training.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant suggested the ice breaker activity "Two Truths and a Lie."
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] In "Two Truths and a Lie," each participant comes up with three statements about themselves: two true and one false.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Other participants have to guess which statement is the lie in the "Two Truths and a Lie" activity.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant noted that this activity encourages communication and interaction among participants.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant mentioned that the activity can be modified to suit the group's preferences, such as sharing favorite hobbies or memorable vacations.
- [USER] User requested another ice breaker.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant suggested another ice breaker activity called "Who Am I?"
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] In "Who Am I?", a name of a famous person, fictional character, or historical figure is written on a sticky note and placed on each participant's forehead.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Each participant must ask yes or no questions to figure out who they are in the "Who Am I?" activity.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant described "Who Am I?" as a fun and engaging way to break the ice and encourage conversation.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant noted that "Who Am I?" encourages creative thinking and problem-solving.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant mentioned that the activity can be modified to use famous quotes or song lyrics instead of famous people.
